Implementation in `agents/librarian/librarian.ts` enforces read-only exploration via `run_terminal_command` shell utilities, explicitly blocking project directory writes and standard file tools that cannot access `/tmp`.

eli5.text: The system now includes a new assistant that can copy any public GitHub project into a temporary folder on your computer and then answer your questions about how that project is organized or what its documentation says, all without changing the original project. You give it a GitHub link and a question, it brings the project to you for reading, and tells you which specific files hold the answers so you can clean up afterward. The assistant is limited to reading files and searching through them, and it cannot write to or modify the original project files.

ai.title: Fix paste events not firing when multiline input loses focus
ai.summary: MultilineInput now registers a global paste listener on `keyHandler` instead of relying solely on the scrollbox `onPaste` prop, ensuring drag-and-drop pastes are captured even when the terminal lacks focus. A backup scrollbox handler with microtask-based deduplication prevents double-processing. The `StdinParser` timeout is increased from 10ms to 100ms to prevent bracketed paste sequence corruption in terminals like Ghostty and iTerm2 that split sequences across reads.

eli5.text: When you paste text (especially by dragging a file into the terminal from your file manager), it now reliably appears in the multiline input field instead of sometimes being ignored. This works because the input now listens for paste events even when the terminal has lost focus during a drag-and-drop, using a backup handler with a short delay to prevent the paste from being processed twice. If you paste while the terminal is not focused, the text will now correctly show up in the input area.

ai.summary: The version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json was incremented from 0.0.17 to 0.0.18 as part of the standard CLI release packaging step. This is a packaging-only release-bump commit with no changes to source code, CLI behavior, or user-facing features. The 0.0.17 release ships the previously integrated e2e:knowledge-file npm script, the CanopyWave prompt caching benchmark tooling, the consolidated basher agent (renamed from commander and commander-lite), and paste-to-attach file handling in the CLI. No migration, environment variable, or developer action is required for this version bump itself.
ai.evidence: The diff in freebuff/cli/release/package.json shows only a version field change from "0.0.16" to "0.0.17" (single line, +1/-1). No code files are modified in this commit. Per analysis notes, this is a release-bump packaging commit; the accompanying release updates (0.0.17 features relative to 0.0.16) are detailed in the commit metadata, not introduced by this hunk itself.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.17 adds powerful new ways to work with codebases, attach files more easily, and get faster visual feedback from agents, all while making automated testing more reliable. You can now paste file paths directly into the chat to attach them, with a preview card showing up and a 'processing attachments...' notice that prevents you from sending a half-attached message. A new librarian agent can clone any GitHub repository into a temporary folder and answer questions about its code structure or documentation, then hand back the files it found so your project directory stays clean. When subagents are actively working, they now show a shimmering 'working...' animation so you can see they're processing instead of frozen, and that indicator automatically hides in collapsed views to reduce clutter. Under the hood, the app's terminal rendering engine was upgraded for smoother text display, slash commands like /interview and /plan got reordered for better autocomplete flow, and a new test suite checks how knowledge files behave. Startup is now more stable in automated tests and paste events are far more reliable in terminals like Ghostty and iTerm2, which used to drop pasted content when the input wasn't fully focused. Upgrading gives you a noticeably more responsive and trustworthy coding assistant, with fewer mysterious blank spots during agent activity and a much easier way to bring files into conversations.

ai.title: Strip ANSI paste and route copy through renderer OSC 52
ai.summary: Paste handlers in cli/src/utils/strings.ts and cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts strip ANSI escape sequences via Bun.stripANSI before processing clipboard or event text. cli/src/utils/clipboard.ts adds registerClipboardRenderer/unregisterClipboardRenderer so copyTextToClipboard prefers renderer.copyToClipboardOSC52 before manual OSC 52 and platform tools. Scope is CLI only: use-clipboard.ts registers the renderer on mount, clipboard.ts and strings.ts carry the logic. tryCopyViaRenderer returns false when no renderer is registered, preserving existing fallback chains.

eli5.text: When you paste text into the CLI app, the app now strips out hidden formatting characters that can come along with copied content, so what you paste looks clean instead of garbled. Similarly, when something gets copied, the app tries to use the terminal's built-in copy feature first before falling back to other methods, which makes copying to your system clipboard more reliable in remote sessions. These changes affect anyone using the CLI tool, especially in SSH or remote environments.

ai.title: Freebuff release blocked by e2e tests
ai.summary: The freebuff-release workflow now requires passing e2e tests before creating a release. This is achieved by adding an e2e-tests job that calls the freebuff-e2e workflow and updating the create-release job's needs. The e2e workflow was modified to support being called by other workflows (workflow_call) and to ensure concurrency groups are unique per caller. This ensures only verified code is released.

eli5.text: When you publish a new version of the freebuff command-line tool, it now has to sit through a full end-to-end test run first, and only if every check passes does the release button get pressed. Previously the release could be created even if those tests hadn't finished or had failed, so this is the safety net that stops a half-baked build from going out. If you watched the process, you'd simply see an extra waiting step appear between the build artifacts and the final release, and the whole sequence would either clear that step or stop there instead of skipping to the end.

ai.title: build-binary.ts searches repoRoot for OpenTUI core bundle
ai.summary: Refactored `patchOpenTuiAssetPaths` in `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts` to locate the `@opentui/core` package in either `cli/node_modules` or `repoRoot/node_modules`. Added `findOpenTuiCoreDir` and `findOpenTuiCoreBundlePath` helpers. The bundle lookup now prefers hashed files (e.g., `index-<hash>.js`) over generic `index.js`. This ensures the tree-sitter asset path patching works correctly in monorepo setups where dependencies are hoisted.

eli5.text: When you build the terminal tool from its source code, the build process now correctly finds the OpenTUI core package even when project dependencies are shared or moved in a monorepo setup. Previously, it only looked in one specific folder (cli/node_modules), which could fail if the package was hoisted to the top-level node_modules. Now it checks both locations and prefers the latest hashed bundle file (like index-abcd1234.js) over the generic index.js, ensuring the tree-sitter asset path patching works in all monorepo configurations. This is a behind-the-scenes fix that makes the build more reliable for developers working on the project.
